title: Focus handoff and roving a11y proposals
content:
Overview:

This is a working doc for the Console design system team that consolidates proposals and lightweight wireframe notes for: focus handoff between UI regions, a roving tabindex strategy for complex toolbars and lists, and a set of accessibility acceptance criteria we can add to the backlog (and component unit tests). The aim is to reduce keyboard friction in multi-pane editor flows (routes list -> editor -> action rail), improve screen reader announcements for dynamic updates, and standardize token adoption for focus/focus-visible states.

Context / problem statements (short):
- Users (keyboard-first and assistive tech) are losing context when focus shifts between panes during actions like "Open route", "Clone model", and "Split view".
- We have multiple ad-hoc implementations of roster/toolbars: some use tabindex=0 on each button, others hide/unhide DOM which sometimes drops focus.
- Modals and flyouts inconsistently return focus when dismissed; some components trap focus incorrectly.
- Our token for focus outline is inconsistent across components and sometimes fails color contrast checks against dark backgrounds.

Goals / success metrics:
- Consistent focus handoff behaviour across console flows; measurable by e2e keyboard tests and UX checklist.
- Reduce reported keyboard-navigation bugs by 70% in next quarter for Console flows in user testing.
- All interactive components pass WCAG 2.1 AA keyboard and screen reader checks; critical components aim for AAA where feasible (contrasts for focus indicators).

Scope (in-scope):
- Toolbar and list components in console (route list, model list, file tree, action rail)
- Modal/flyout focus return patterns
- Roving tabindex pattern for composite toolbars and list of selectable items
- Focus-visible tokenization and contrast audit for focus/focus-ring states

Out-of-scope (for this doc):
- Full-page reflow animations (separate perf/ops work)
- Mobile-specific touch gestures (will be handled later)

Wireframe notes (sketch-level):
- Left pane (routes list) -> center (editor) -> right rail (actions): keyboard tab order should be linear across panes unless user used arrow nav inside a composite. Example flows:
  * Tab into routes list: first focus lands on search input (tabindex default), arrow keys move up/down the list (roving tabindex), Enter opens route and puts focus into editor title; if editor open, focus should land on the H1 editable title with an explicit focus-visible state.
  * From editor to action rail: pressing F6 (or configurable shortcut) moves focus from editor content to next region (action rail) to avoid losing place in long forms.
- Modal dismiss: escape closes modal and focus returns to the element that triggered the modal (store trigger element in data attribute when opening).

Proposed patterns (detailed):
1) Roving tabindex for lists and toolbars
  - Each composite (toolbar, selectable list) maintains exactly one tabbable element (tabindex=0), all other children use tabindex=-1.
  - Arrow keys move the tabindex=0 to next/previous focusable child and internally call element.focus().
  - Home/End jump to first/last item.
  - Roving component exposes high-level props: ariaOrientation (horizontal|vertical) and selectionMode (none|single|multi).
  - Suggested implementation notes for engineers: keep a small internal focusIndex state, but not rely on DOM order changes for accessibility. When items are added/removed, attempt to maintain focusIndex by matching id or fallback to nearest index.

2) Focus handoff between panes and full-screen editor
  - Use region landmarks (role="region" + aria-label) for major panes. When user activates an item that opens a different region, call focus on the primary interactive element in the destination region and issue an aria-live polite message with short context (e.g., "Route editor opened for: checkout-page").
  - If activation happened via keyboard (detect by last input technique pointer), set focus and do not change scroll unexpectedly.
  - Preference: preserve selection focus when returning to source pane (remember the previously active child id).

3) Modals/flyouts focus return
  - On open: save document.activeElement to data attribute on the modal container.
  - On close: if saved element still in DOM, restore focus. If not, fall back to a nearby focusable element (e.g., the toolbar button that triggered the modal).
  - Avoid focusing the body; prefer interactive elements.

4) Focus-visible tokens and contrast rules
  - Define tokens: token-focus-ring, token-focus-outline, token-focus-bg-weak.
  - Recommend usage: token-focus-ring: 2px solid color with shadow; token-focus-outline for thin one-pixel outlines on compact components.
  - Contrast requirement: outer ring color must be >= 3:1 contrast vs background when component is adjacent to content (aim AA for non-text UI components). For key text targets (e.g., editable title), ensure focus ring plus background gives perceived contrast >= 4.5:1 against adjacent content.
  - Example tokens (proposal):
    * token-focus-ring: #3B82F6 (blue-500) on light backgrounds, fallback to #60A5FA on dark surfaces; contrast against white = 3.9:1.
    * token-focus-outline: #111827 (neutral-900) on light surfaces when using inverted backgrounds.

Contrast audit snapshot (quick checks done using lighthouse/axe on sample screens):
- Primary button focus ring (current): #2563EB on white -> contrast 4.0:1 (passes AA for non-text)
- Compact icon-only toolbar (current): 1px blue outline on white -> contrast 2.3:1 (FAIL)
- Suggested action: increase thickness to 2px or add subtle box-shadow to reach >3:1

Acceptance criteria (component-level):
- RovingToolbar v1: keyboard navigation arrow keys, Home/End support, role=toolbar, aria-orientation set, unit tests for focus movement, e2e keyboard scenario: pass.
- SelectableList v1: supports single and multi selection with roving tabindex and aria-activedescendant fallback for virtualized lists.
- Modal component: always restores focus to trigger on close; escape key closes; focus never lands outside the modal while open.

Backlog groom (priority buckets + owners):
- P0 (this sprint):
  * CON-4821 - Add roving tabindex to routes list and toolbar (owner: Miguel Torres)
  * CON-4823 - Modal focus-return bugfix surfaced in customer report (owner: Leah Kim)
- P1 (next sprint):
  * CON-4870 - Design token adjustments for focus ring contrast and tests (owner: Design System)
  * CON-4899 - Keyboard shortcut F6 discovery and registration (owner: Rohit Singh)
- P2:
  * CON-4952 - Screen reader verbosity tuning for aria-live updates (owner: Product UX)

Meeting notes (from 2026-07-12 working session):
- Alignment: team agreed on roving tabindex default for all internal composite components.
- Disagreement: whether to expose roving tabindex as an opt-in or opt-out API. Action: default should be opt-in for external-facing components with clear migration docs.
- Action items: Miguel to prototype with virtualized list (important for model list). Leah to run accessibility smoke tests on current modals by EOD Friday.

Open questions / risks:
- Virtualized lists (windowing): aria-activedescendant vs physical focus movement tradeoffs. Prefer aria-activedescendant for huge lists to avoid DOM focus churn, but that requires careful announcement handling.
- Keyboard shortcut conflicts with browser or OS (F6 recommendation is a suggestion only). Need list of reserved keys and mapping table.
- Internationalization: some screen reader phrasing may be too verbose in non-English locales; we need translations for aria-live messages.

Engineering notes / pseudo snippets:
- Roving tabindex pseudocode:
  const items = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('[data-roving-item]'))
  let focusIndex = Math.max(0, previouslySavedIndex || 0)
  function setIndex(i) {
    items.forEach((it, idx) => it.tabIndex = idx === i ? 0 : -1)
    items[i].focus()
  }
  container.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    if (e.key === 'ArrowDown') setIndex((focusIndex+1) % items.length)
    if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') setIndex((focusIndex-1+items.length) % items.length)
  })

- Modal open/close focus save:
  const trigger = document.activeElement
  openModal() { modal.dataset.triggerId = trigger.id || '' }
  closeModal() { const t = document.getElementById(modal.dataset.triggerId); t?.focus() }

Testing checklist (manual + automated):
- Manual:
  * Tab through the three-pane flows in dev and confirm tab stops are intuitive and predictable.
  * Test with VoiceOver and NVDA: ensure activation announces destination and context.
  * Test focus return for modals opened from dynamic lists where the trigger may be removed.
- Automated:
  * Cypress keyboard tests for roving components.
  * Axe checks in CI with focused contrast assertions.

Next steps (owner, due):
- Prototype: Miguel (2026-07-22) -> small PR with roving tabindex and unit tests for routes list.
- Token update proposal: Design System (Leah) (2026-07-24) -> include contrast measurements and suggested color swatches.
- Docs: Draft migration guide for component maintainers (Aisha) (2026-07-30)

Notes to self: remember to surface the virtualized-list aria-activedescendant caveat in the PR description and link the example from Material/WAI examples. Also jot down possible accessibility regressions in the release notes so customers with assistive tech are warned.

---

This is a working document — interpret as a mix of spec + implementation notes. Will iterate after prototyping and the next UX review.
